subject: Clarifying buyer identity requirements and term windows for Private Offer (BrightPay)
messages:
From: Alicia Jones <alicia@brightpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer: Term options & who can sign

Hi Sean —

Quick one from procurement as we pull together a Private Offer on AWS Marketplace. Two questions: 1) BrightPay prefers an 18-month committed term (budgeting cycle) — can Redwood issue PO/private-offer with an 18-month term, or do you only do 12/24? 2) Who needs to be the buyer on the Private Offer? We have a corporate AWS account (see below) but sometimes our CFO wants the PO on a different legal entity in the same org. Will that create issues for AWS processing or co-sell?

AWS account id: 123456789012
Attached: BrightPay_RFP.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — appreciate a quick read.

— Alicia Jones
Procurement Director, BrightPay
attachment: BrightPay_RFP.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Jones <alicia@brightpay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: Term options & who can sign

Hi Alicia — thanks for the RFP and the clear questions. Short answers up top, details below: 1) We can support 12- or 24-month private offer terms by default. 18 months is possible but requires approval from our commercial operations/legal team because it falls outside our standard cadence. 2) The buyer on the Private Offer must match an AWS account that can accept the offer (AWS buyer account id). If you need the PO tied to a different legal entity, we can do that, but AWS will want documentation that the entity is authorized to accept on behalf of the corporate account.

Details / next steps:
- If you can confirm the exact legal entity name as it appears in AWS and the target AWS account ID, I can start the private-offer workflow.
- For 18 months, please confirm whether you need price smoothing (annual payment) or a one-time prepaid PO. The commercial team will evaluate pricing for non-standard lengths; if approved, it typically comes with a fixed-discount threshold.
- For co-sell eligibility: to preserve the marketplace co-sell signal, the buyer must be visible in the Marketplace record. Consolidated billing is fine but we need a short authorization letter if the PO is issued by a different legal entity.

Attaching our internal checklist (redwood-private-offer-checklist.pdf) so you can see the items we’ll route through procurement/legal once you confirm.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
attachment: redwood-private-offer-checklist.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Jones <alicia@brightpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: Term options & who can sign

Alicia — quick note from the co-sell side. If BrightPay wants co-sell enabled on the Private Offer, we need the offer to reference the buyer AWS account directly (the one Sean noted). Co-sell also requires a short partner-intent form inside the AWS console; we can help you with that.

From a product/ops perspective we usually recommend 12 months + optional renewal (simpler for usage and forecasting). If you must do 18 months for budgetary reasons, we can try to structure it as an 18-month commitment split into two billing milestones (year-1 and remainder), which helps reconcile internal BrightPay finance rules. I’ll coordinate with BizOps if Sean gets the green light to pursue 18 months.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Confirming details from our side: BrightPay Corporate (legal name: BrightPay Holdings Ltd) will be the payer on the PO. AWS account id: 123456789012 (attached to our billing entity). We are trying to sync the procurement cycle with an 18-month commitment — ideally annual invoicing but committed for 18 months.

Can Redwood provide an eligibility statement for co-sell and confirm whether an 18-month term will materially change discount levels? We’re fine sending an auth letter if necessary.

Our HubSpot record: HS-9876 (includes finance contact and legal contact).

Thanks —
Alicia

Alicia — thanks for the confirmation and HubSpot link. Internal note (keeping you on copy for transparency): I’m approving the 18-month private offer for BrightPay with the following commercial guardrails:

- Approved term: 18 months (one-off approval)
- Discount: 10% off list for the 18-month commit (conditional on PO issuance and signed terms)
- Billing: annual invoicing at the start of year 1, remainder invoiced at month 13 (we’ll draft payment milestones in the contract)
- Co-sell: Eligible; Redwood will submit the co-sell nomination after the private offer is live. We’ll need the authorization letter if the payer entity differs from the usage account (please upload to HubSpot HS-9876).

Next actions for BrightPay: please upload the signed PO and authorization letter to HS-9876 and confirm billing contact. Once received, Sean will create the AWS private offer and route to our legal for the PO terms (PO_Terms_v2.pdf attached). We’ll send a DocuSign envelope for signatures: https://docusign.net/some-ds-link/abc123

SEAN — please create the private offer in AWS for account 123456789012 and loop in Kimberly for legal review on the PO terms. Vanessa, please prepare the co-sell nomination once the offer is visible.

Thanks all,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
